module.title: Constrained and contact dynamics with the Delassus operator
module.expensive_path: Forming and factorizing the Delassus operator, the inverse articulated inertia projected onto the constraint space, and solving the resulting saddle-point system for constraint forces and accelerations. The contact-space Cholesky is the per-step cost of any simulator built on this code, and it must be rebuilt every time the configuration changes. A physics step in a contact-rich scene spends most of its time here, and batching independent scenes is the acceleration target that GPU simulators exploit.
module.rationale: Constraints change the physics: the equations of motion acquire a Lagrange-multiplier block, and a different family of algorithms (constrained ABA, the proximal and primal-dual formulations, the loop-constrained ABA for closed chains, impulse dynamics for collisions) is needed to solve them. The module is cut at the boundary where a constraint set is given and the dynamics must be solved for it, leaving what a constraint is and how a frictional cone is projected to its own module.
excluded: the constraint model library and the frictional cone solvers, which are the contact-solvers module
unconstrained forward and inverse dynamics, which are the rigid-body-algorithms module
hazards: Proximal and primal-dual formulations carry regularisation parameters and an iteration count; the iteration count is bookkeeping and must never be graded.
The contact-space Cholesky involves ordering choices that a correct port may legitimately change, so the graded quantity is the resulting forces and accelerations, not the factor.
Two of these tests (contact-dynamics-derivatives) load a robot description from the example-robot-data submodule.
Shares the unseeded-model hazard recorded on rigid-body-algorithms: buildModels::humanoidRandom randomises placements, inertias and limits from std::rand, so the model must be frozen as data in ic/.
